thread:
samir: AcmePayments reporting intermittent 503s this morning, peak around 09:12 UTC. They say dedicated pool didn't scale fast enough.
opsbot: alert: AcmePayments-dedicated-pool high 5xx rate (90s window) :warning:
maya: noting customer impact, they've opened a case — severity 2. Getting stack traces and request IDs.
jordan: @samir can you post the pool config and any hpa/hc logs?
samir: grabbing details now. their dedicated pool is `dedicated-acme-east1`, minReplicas=2, maxReplicas=12, nodePool=highmem-preemptible.
samir: tried `kubectl get hpa dedicated-acme-east1 -o yaml` and saw cpu metric spike but scale up events were sparse.
samir: relevant bits from controller log: 
```
I0317 09:12:35 controller.go:123] HPA dedicated-acme-east1 desiredReplicas 2 -> 8 (reason: metrics > target)
I0317 09:12:40 scale_up.go:87] scale-up suppressed: recentScaleDown=true cooldown
I0317 09:15:12 scale_up.go:118] nodeProvisioner: insufficient capacity in nodePool highmem-preemptible
```
leah: interesting — cooldown blocked the immediate ramp, and node provisioning delayed because of preemptibles.
maya: customer says errors started at 09:11 and lasted ~6 minutes, a few dozen 503s then fell back. They hit a couple of 429s too while requests queued.
jordan: can we repro in staging? steps to reproduce and quick checks?
samir: repro steps I ran: 
1) fire concurrent 200 RPS synthetic to `acme-pay/api/v1/charge` with realistic token sizes
2) observe pod CPU and HPA.
I ran it and HPA wanted to go to 9 but stayed at 2-3 for ~3m because cluster-autoscaler couldn't get nodes fast enough.
leah: cluster-autoscaler logs show scale-up attempt but cloud quota and image pull times delayed node readiness. Also saw one pod failing readiness check for ~180s due to slow KV cache warmup.
samir: past incidents had warmup ~30s; this was 3m because quantized model downloads started on init and saturated disk bandwidth.
maya: customer worried about auth errors in same window — they saw repeated `401` on retry. Any correlation?
jordan: `401` likely from token refresh race during 503s; retries hit auth backend rate limits. Separate but related.
leah: short-term mitigation I'd suggest: bump minReplicas to 4 for this pool, change nodePool to non-preemptible for steady hours, and reduce HPA cooldown (scaleUp stabilization) to allow faster ramp. Also add a small burst pool.
samir: I pushed a test change to increase minReplicas to 4 and requested instance type change for their dedicated pool in staging.
samir: commands used: 
```
kubectl patch hpa dedicated-acme-east1 -p '{"spec":{"minReplicas":4}}'
# then monitor
kubectl get hpa dedicated-acme-east1 -w
```
deploy-bot: deployment: dedicated-acme-east1 config patch applied by samir at 09:28 UTC :white_check_mark:
maya: FYI opened INC-2026-3247 and assigned to eng-infra; notifying Acme rep and giving temporary SLA credit.
jordan: long-term: we should add pre-warmed spare nodes for high-SLO dedicated pools and a metric that blocks preemptible selection if expected scale-up latency > 60s.
leah: also need to add a warmup probe for model loads and fail fast if downloads contend; we can parallelize fetching.
samir: I've attached the minimal repro script in the thread (link to gist). For now Acme confirmed fewer errors after minReplicas bump.
maya: customer thanked support, asked for RCA timeline.
jordan: I'll own the RCA, will include: (1) HPA cooldown interaction, (2) nodePool preemptible fragility, (3) slow model warmup on pod init, (4) retry/auth surge.
leah: follow-ups: adjust autoscaler thresholds, add prewarm pool, and add a dashboard to show predicted scale-up time vs. request latency.
maya: closing loop with customer today, will share interim mitigations. :thumbsup:
samir: notes saved to INC-2026-3247. will follow up with logs and exact timestamps.
opsbot: alert resolved: AcmePayments-dedicated-pool error rate returned to normal at 09:35 UTC :white_check_mark:
jordan: thanks everyone — adding this to next infra retro to avoid repeating. :eyes:
